examples.sql: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "countrylanguage"."CountryCode" AS e, "country"."Continent" AS g, AVG("countrylanguage"."Percentage") AS m1 FROM "countrylanguage" JOIN "country" ON "country"."Code" = "countrylanguage"."CountryCode"  GROUP BY "countrylanguage"."CountryCode", "country"."Continent"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS g, AVG("s1"."m1") AS v FROM "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS e, "s1"."g" AS g, "s1"."m1" AS m1, ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS m2 FROM "s1" JOIN "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS v FROM "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS e, "s3"."g" AS g, "s3"."m1" AS m1, "s3"."m2" AS m2, (CAST("s3"."m2" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") AS m3 FROM "s3" JOIN "s4" ON "s4"."v" IS NOT NULL), "s6" AS (SELECT "s5"."g" AS g, AVG("s5"."m1") AS m1, AVG("s5"."m2") AS m2, AVG("s5"."m3") AS m3 FROM "s5" GROUP BY "s5"."g") SELECT AVG("s6"."m1") AS m1, AVG("s6"."m2") AS m2, AVG("s6"."m3") AS m3 FROM "s6"
examples.instruction:
Step 1. Start from each `countrylanguage` record; combine it with each `country` record for which Code (`country.Code`) equals Country Code (`countrylanguage.CountryCode`) (compared as text, character by character), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); group the kept records by Country Code (`countrylanguage.CountryCode`) and continent (`country.Continent`); each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) Country Code (`countrylanguage.CountryCode`); (2) continent (`country.Continent`); (3) the average of share of country population speaking language (`countrylanguage.Percentage`) in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 2. Start from the rows of step 1; group the kept records by column (2) of step 1; each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) column (2) of step 1; (2) the average of column (3) of step 1 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 3. Start from the rows of step 1; combine it with the rows of step 2 for which column (2) of step 1 equals column (1) of step 2 (compared as text, character by character), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); keep only the records for which column (3) of step 1 is greater than column (2) of step 2; for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 1; (2) column (2) of step 1; (3) column (3) of step 1; (4) A − B. Here A is column (3) of step 1; B is column (2) of step 2.
Step 4. Start from the rows of step 3; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the average of column (4) of step 3 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 5. Start from the rows of step 3; combine it with the rows of step 4 for which it is not true that column (1) of step 4 is missing, one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 3; (2) column (2) of step 3; (3) column (3) of step 3; (4) column (4) of step 3; (5) A ÷ B. Here A is column (4) of step 3; B is column (1) of step 4.
Step 6. Start from the rows of step 5; group the kept records by column (2) of step 5; each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) column (2) of step 5; (2) the average of column (3) of step 5 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (3) the average of column (4) of step 5 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (4) the average of column (5) of step 5 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 7 (the answer). Start from the rows of step 6; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the average of column (2) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (2) the average of column (3) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (3) the average of column (4) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
